fatal_errors: The proposed intervention is ab initio molecular dynamics rather than controlled chemical short-range ordering in random bcc HfNbTaTiZr.
It misses the target mechanism of reduced lattice distortion and formation of conductive, percolating HfTi/TiZr ordered-cluster pathways.
It predicts an unexplained 10–20% reduction in predicted conductivity, whereas the target predicts an approximately 12% conductivity increase relative to the random alloy.
A lower predicted value is incorrectly treated as evidence of greater predictive accuracy without comparison to a validated reference.
The benchmark does not vary or quantify short-range order, atomic displacement reduction, percolation, or phonon-density-of-states changes.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses phonon thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys and proposes a generally testable simulation-versus-experiment comparison, but it does not reconstruct the material, intervention, mechanism, or outcome of the target study. Its DFT/AIMD rationale is broadly plausible, yet no evidence supports the claimed 10–20% improvement, and compositionally disordered alloys pose finite-size and configurational-sampling limitations not captured by the stated boundary. The 30% falsification threshold is measurable but weak and cannot distinguish the target SRO/percolation mechanism from generic model error.
